slot.brief: Order given radicals or carbocations by stability, possibly including benzylic/allylic vs alkyl, and pick the correct decreasing-stability sequence.

stem: Arrange the following free radicals in decreasing order of stability: benzyl, allyl, tert-butyl and ethyl.

verdicts.working: Benzyl and allyl radicals are resonance-stabilized, with benzyl more stable; among the alkyl radicals, tert-butyl is more stable than ethyl due to greater hyperconjugation. Thus benzyl > allyl > tert-butyl > ethyl.

working:
Resonance stabilisation: benzyl $>$ allyl. Hyperconjugation stabilises alkyl radicals as $3^\circ>1^\circ$; hence tert-butyl $>$ ethyl. Overall: benzyl $>$ allyl $>$ tert-butyl $>$ ethyl.
